problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}).$ What are the polar coordinates of $P?$

feedback.problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(-a,a),$ where $a$ is a positive real number. What are the polar coordinates of $P?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-a)^{2}+{a}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2{a}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\text{ }\,a.\end{aligned}
$$

For the reference angle, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{-a})| \\  & =|-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)| \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies in the second quadrant, we subtract the reference angle from $\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are  $(\sqrt{2}\text{ }\,a,\frac{3\pi }{4}).$
